sections.h2: Augusta County and its independent cities
sections.html:
Augusta County lies in the Shenandoah Valley, on Virginia's western side. Covering 971 square miles, it is among the biggest counties in the state, and the 2020 census counted 77,487 residents. Craigsville and Grottoes are the two towns, and Stuarts Draft, Fishersville and Verona are the larger unincorporated communities.

The county encircles the independent cities of Staunton and Waynesboro, which are separate governments. That split decides who sends your bill. A Staunton or Waynesboro mailing address can mean a city tax bill, while a house just beyond the city line answers to Augusta County. The parcel location decides it, not the community name on an envelope, so check the county assessment records or phone the offices before assuming.

Two equal installments come due, on June 5 and December 5. A weekend date slides to the following Monday. You may also pay the whole year in June. Bills can be viewed and paid on the county's e-Treasurer site.

InstallmentDue dateIf paid late
First halfJune 510 percent penalty plus 10 percent yearly interest
Second halfDecember 5Same penalty and interest
Whole year at onceJuneNo second bill follows

The penalty is applied to the unpaid balance, and interest runs on whatever stays unpaid. The state's share of personal property tax is left out of the interest.

sections.h2: When Augusta County waives a late charge
sections.html:
Owners carry the responsibility of knowing their due dates. If a bill never arrives, reach the taxing office ahead of the deadline and set up payment. Several excuses never work: not knowing the date, receiving no bill, a bill sent to a wrong address, an incorrect bill, or bad information from county staff.

A waiver is possible in narrower situations.

  • A medically determinable physical or mental impairment on the due date, followed by payment within 30 days.
  • The Commissioner of the Revenue abates the tax or certifies a clerical error in that office.
  • The Treasurer or the Commissioner of the Revenue was the only cause of the delay.

An owner unable to pay everything can arrange a payment plan through the Treasurer's Office, (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us. The plan leaves the penalty standing, and interest continues.

The Board of Supervisors sets the rate. Its 2024 figure was $0.52 per $100 of assessed value, applied to values the Real Estate Assessor's Office sets as of January 1. Your latest bill shows the rate in force now.

Values are redone every five years. The latest round started in September 2022 and sent notices in February 2024. The county brought in Wampler-Eanes Appraisal Group, which split the county into about 96 neighborhoods and visited accessible properties to verify records and refresh property cards and photos.

A county review of 2023 home sales covered 680 sales and found a median rise of 58.3 percent over the old assessment. Beverly Manor (69.5 percent) and North River (68.8 percent) saw the biggest median jumps. Craigsville (33.7 percent, from only three sales) saw the smallest.

Many owners were startled by the new numbers. An assessment is the county's estimate and not a sale price, so test yours against what buyers are paying near you.

The county outlines three stages: an informal hearing with the assessor, then the Board of Equalization, then Circuit Court. Informal requests have been accepted by Zoom, phone, email, mail or in person.

  • Reasons the county names: value that looks high or low, uneven values among similar homes, changed condition, comparable sales and clerical mistakes.
  • Deadlines depend on your notice, so work from the dates printed on it.

Virginia Code section 58.1-3381 lets the board raise, lower or uphold a value, and the owner gets advance notice before any increase. Once in court under section 58.1-3984, the assessor's number is treated as right, and the owner has to overcome it with a greater weight of evidence.

A tax debt stays attached to the house. Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 gives real estate a tax lien that stands first until it is paid, and money from the sale goes toward that tax. The contract determines how the current year is divided between buyer and seller.

The deed carries costs too. The seller usually pays the grantor tax in section 58.1-802, fifty cents for each $500, unless the parties agree otherwise. The state recordation tax in section 58.1-801 is 25 cents per $100. State law in section 58.1-3916 sets a ceiling on late charges, a penalty of 10 percent of overdue tax or $10 if that is more, plus 10 percent yearly interest, which are the figures Augusta County uses.

Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer before closing, and keep the receipt for the title company. An unpaid balance is something we can work through with you, because we purchase houses in their current condition.

sections.h2: Before you list an Augusta County house
sections.html:
1. Look up the parcel in the county assessment records and confirm which locality bills it.
  2. Check the 2024 value against recent sales near you.
  3. Call the Treasurer for the balance on both installments.
  4. Ask about a payment plan if the balance is more than you can cover at once.
  5. Collect the payoff letter and receipts for your closing agent.

An owner whose job or a relative's care pulls them out of the area can sell for cash and skip a long financing process.

faqs.q: Are Staunton and Waynesboro part of Augusta County?
faqs.a: No. They are independent cities that Augusta County surrounds. A house inside either city is generally handled by the city, so check which office bills you.

faqs.q: When are Augusta County property taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. A weekend due date slides to the following Monday.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Augusta County?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty on the unpaid balance and 10 percent annual interest. A payment plan does not remove either charge.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about a payment plan?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Office at (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us.

faqs.q: How many years between Augusta County reassessments?
faqs.a: Five. The latest reassessment took effect in 2024.
